title: Why Is Wall Street Doubting Google Stock?
detail:
Why Is Wall Street Doubting Google Stock?
Trefis Team
Thu, August 27, 2026 at 4:39 PM PDT 4 min read
NFLX
GOOG
AAPL
AMZN
SPGI
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Photo by PawinG on Pixabay

After a sharp pullback, one of the world's most dominant companies is trading at a steep discount to the market, forcing investors to decide if they are looking at a bargain or a warning sign.

Alphabet (GOOGL), the digital titan behind Google Search and YouTube, trades at 17.0 times earnings while the S&P 500 median sits at 23.5. That discount follows a real markdown; the stock is 15% below its 52-week high. Yet even with that pullback, shares have returned +65% over the past year, handily beating the S&P 500's +20% gain. The numbers present a paradox for bargain hunters. Is this a rare chance to own a quality business for less, or is the market correctly pricing in a coming storm?

 The Business Is Firing On All Cylinders.

The case for value begins with operational strength. A quantitative screen for signs of a deteriorating business comes up empty. Alphabet's revenue over the last twelve months grew 20%, more than double the S&P 500 median of 8.4%, and comfortably outpacing its own three-year average of 15.5%. Profitability is elite, not merely intact. The company's operating margin over the last twelve months was 33%, far outpacing the S&P 500 median of 18.5%.

This performance is reflected across the business. The latest quarterly results show the growth engine is broad-based. The core Search and other segment grew 17%, YouTube ads climbed 13%, and the Google Cloud division posted a stunning 82% revenue increase. This performance is powered by what management calls "strong demand for AI infrastructure and AI solutions," a sign that its large investments are finding a receptive market.

The Market Is Pricing In The Cost Of An AI Arms Race.

If the business is so healthy, why the discount? The market's anxiety centers on the large cost of competing in artificial intelligence. Alphabet's stepped-up capital investments resulted in a negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion. Management has also raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to a range of $195 billion to $205 billion, warning that free cash flow will "remain under pressure."

This spending spree fuels the central worry for skeptics: that Alphabet is paying a fortune to potentially fall behind. On its latest earnings call, analysts pressed management on the "speed of model releases" and whether its Gemini models can "remain at the frontier" against fast-moving competitors. The concern among some market observers is whether frontier AI investments will generate sufficient returns to justify the elevated capital intensity.

title: How Much Track Is Left For SNOW Stock?
detail:
How Much Track Is Left For SNOW Stock?
Trefis Team
Thu, August 27, 2026 at 4:14 PM PDT 4 min read
SNOW
ORCL-PD
AMZN
GOOG
PLTR
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image by Gerd Altmann from Pixabay

A powerful business engine has fueled this data stock's long-term run, but a recent pullback forces every investor to ask if the ticket price already accounts for the journey ahead.

Snowflake (SNOW) has been a genuine runner, the kind of stock that makes you feel you are missing out. Its long-term trend strength ranks in the top 7% of large U.S. stocks. But the fear of chasing a hot name is met with an immediate reality check: the stock is not at its peak. It trades about 7% below its 52-week high and has pulled back about 7% from its one-month high, so the weakness is fresh. The stock also sits about 7% below its two-year high of $337.38. This presents the classic momentum question for any would-be buyer: is this a brief pause in a powerful climb, or has the market already priced in all the good news? Momentum with fuel, or momentum fully priced?

This run is powered by a real business engine.

The source of Snowflake's momentum extends beyond its stock chart. The company's AI Data Cloud platform is seeing surging demand as enterprises race to deploy artificial intelligence. Revenue over the last twelve months grew 31%, a stark contrast to the S&P 500 median of 8.4%. The company is also generating cash, with an operating cash flow margin of 25%, beating the market median of 22%.

The fuel for this is the rapid adoption of new AI-centric products. Management noted on its latest earnings call that tools like Snowflake Intelligence and Cortex Code (CoCo) are seeing "the fastest adoption of any new products in our history." This does more than add a new revenue line; it's creating a flywheel. Customers using these tools are increasing their use of the core data platform, which prompted management to raise its full-year product revenue growth outlook for fiscal 2027 to 31%.

The market charges a steep price for that power.

A buyer today is paying a premium for that growth. Snowflake trades at a price-to-sales multiple of 21.6, far above the S&P 500 median of 3.3. Profitability remains a work in progress; the company's operating margin over the last twelve months is -26%, compared to the S&P 500 median of 18.5%. The market is clearly betting that Snowflake's current investments will translate into future profits.

Beyond being a valuation concern, the honest catch here is a business risk. As one recent analysis notes, there is a question of whether this growth arrives at a lower gross margin. Management confirms its new AI products have a lower gross margin than its core platform. The bigger risk is customer behavior. Investors worry that as clients see their bills rise from the consumption-based pricing of these powerful AI tools, they might "govern or throttle the use" to contain spending. If the cost of innovation outpaces the perceived value, the growth engine could sputter.

title: S&P 500 investors are quietly making a huge shift
detail:
S&P 500 investors are quietly making a huge shift
Damilola Esebame
Thu, August 27, 2026 at 2:17 PM PDT 5 min read
^GSPC
AAPL
MSFT
NVDA
GOOG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

For years, investors have watched a small group of mega-cap companies drive much of the S&P 500's performance.

The Magnificent Seven — Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Tesla — accounted for the bulk of the index's gains, and investors saw little reason to bet against them.

However, that trade stalled in 2026, and the equal-weight version of the S&P 500, which gives every company the same influence regardless of size, is now leading

As of early August, the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP) had returned 13.1% year to date, compared with about 10% for the cap-weighted Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO), according to Benzinga.

RSP surpassed $100 billion in assets under management for the first time in August, after attracting more than $12 billion in net inflows in 2026, CNBC reported. 

That milestone marks the clearest sign yet that investors are repositioning beyond mega-cap dominance.

The Magnificent 7 stall in 2026

Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Tesla collectively lost 1.9% in the first half of 2026, while the broader index gained 9.3%, Bloomberg reported.

That gap reflects a broadening of market leadership beyond the Magnificent Seven, while performance within the group has also diverged sharply. Microsoft was down 18.64% year to date as of July 16, while Apple was up 20.70%. 

Tesla was down 14.15% year to date as of July 16, while rival BYD delivered 557,090 battery-electric vehicles in the second quarter and reclaimed the global BEV sales lead, according to Investing.com. 

Related: Bank of America spots new curveball for Magnificent Seven stocks

The four major hyperscalers, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, and Amazon, are now projected to spend a combined $725 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026, up from earlier estimates of $670 billion, according to Financial Times analysis of the companies' earnings-call guidance.

Brent Thill, a technology equity analyst at Jefferies, called it a "show me" phase, investors want to see that spending translate into profits.

The Magnificent Seven are projected to post 22.8% earnings growth in the fourth quarter of 2026, trailing the 25.3% expected from the other 493 S&P 500 companies, according to FactSet. 

The Magnificent Seven traded at about 25.8 times forward earnings in February, compared with 21.8 times for the S&P 500, according to Yardeni Research.

That underperformance carries added weight because the market entered 2026 unusually concentrated: the 10 largest S&P 500 companies accounted for nearly 40% of the index by mid-2025, a level not seen since the mid-1960s, according to S&P Dow Jones Indices.

title: SentinelOne (S) Q2 Earnings and Revenues Surpass Estimates
detail:
SentinelOne (S) Q2 Earnings and Revenues Surpass Estimates
SentinelOne (S) Q2 Earnings and Revenues Surpass Estimates · Zacks
Zacks Equity Research
Thu, August 27, 2026 at 2:15 PM PDT 3 min read

SentinelOne (S) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.08 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.07 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.04 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +14.29%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this cybersecurity provider would post earnings of $0.02 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.04, delivering a surprise of +100%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

SentinelOne, which belongs to the Zacks Security industry, posted revenues of $291.98 million for the quarter ended July 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 0.67%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $242.18 million. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates three times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

SentinelOne shares have added about 36.7% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 12.1%.

What's Next for SentinelOne?

While SentinelOne has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for SentinelOne was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $0.11 on $309.5 million in revenues for the coming quarter and $0.35 on $1.2 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.
